messages:
anya: quick question — do we want reservation credits to be transferable between burst and steady pools? :thinking:
rohan: short answer: no transfer by default. credits represent committed capacity and accounting. transferring breaks billing guarantees.
kevin: +1 on that, but maybe allow an override for emergency ops with audit trail.
maria: what about soft transfer via temporary loan? i.e., low-latency approval that creates a short-lived lease with higher cost. avoids permanent accounting changes.
anya: exactly what i was imagining. loan semantics could help with spikes without expanding steady pools. tradeoffs still: complexity, race conditions during eviction.
samir: eviction is where most surprises happen. if we loan credits and then evict borrowed slots, who pays the cost of premature evictions? tenant or platform?
rohan: propose policy: loans are paid at a premium by borrower; on eviction within loan window, borrower absorbs cost; platform only covers when we proactively reject due to safety. makes incentives clear.
kevin: sketching a config snippet for the loan policy:
```
loanPolicy:
  enabled: true
  maxDurationSec: 600
  premiumMultiplier: 1.5
  evictionPenalty: "borrower"
  approval: "auto-if-free-burst-credits>threshold"
```
maria: love the explicit fields. question: how do we reason about fairness when many tenants ask for loans simultaneously? priority classes?
anya: yes, we need priority classes + per-tenant credit watermarks. also consider randomized backoff to avoid thundering herd.
samir: operational concern: how will the autoscaler compute desired size when loans are active? we must avoid double-counting loaned capacity as provisioned capacity. i suggest autoscaler sees two buckets: committed (steady) and transient (loans), and only uses committed for prediction windows > 5m.
rohan: agree. for admission control we can accept transient requests up to a global transient cap. that cap should be configurable per-region.
kevin: also add a safety loop: if transient utilization > 80% for >2m, trigger prewarm for steady pools and throttle loans. prevents constant oscillation.
autoscaler-bot: INFO: simulated run with current heuristics shows 12% cost increase under aggressive loans, 35% reduction in 95p latency.
maria: that's promising — ops needs a cost dashboard to show loan usage per-tenant and how much premium charged. visibility is critical for chargeback.
anya: next steps: (1) draft RFC for loan semantics + accounting, (2) prototype approval flow and autoscaler flags, (3) run chaos test with eviction scenarios. volunteers?
rohan: i can draft accounting section.
kevin: i'll prototype autoscaler changes and the transient bucket logic.
samir: i'll own chaos tests and create eviction scenarios.
maria: i'll design chargeback dashboard mockups and metrics.
anya: thanks — i'll assemble RFC skeleton and sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
kevin: filing a short follow-up with proposed config options after lunch.
autoscaler-bot: NOTIFICATION: scheduled simulation run complete. logs at https://ci.redwood/sim/1764129876/loan-policy
anya: perfect, thanks everyone.
